Other words

  • Quīdum? — how so?

    also used · classical · Traupman 101; Traupman 101; Traupman 330

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

  • Quid jam? — how so? how’s that?

    also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 2.3.51: Quid jam? — Quia luscitiōsus. (Lewis & Short s.v. luscitiōsus); Traupman 101; Traupman 111; Traupman 330

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

    In Plautus it asks for a reason and is answered with quia. Traupman 111 glosses it “what (is the trouble) now?”, which it does not mean (see what’s the matter?).

  • Quī istuc? — how come?

    quī, the old ablative “how?”, with istuc · also used · classical · Traupman 100; Traupman 330

    Plautus has quī istuc potis est fierī? (Plaut. Amph. 2.2.62, Lewis & Short s.v. enim); the short form is Traupman’s.

  • Quī fit? — how come? how does it happen (that …)?

    quī, the old ablative “how”, with fit; a clause with ut follows when the thing is named · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.1.1: Quī fit, Maecēnās, ut nēmō … (Lewis & Short s.v. sors); Traupman 184

See also why not?, really?.
